mechanical: Stress uses branch-specific nominal effective area; strain uses declared initial gauge/height
Engaged linear fit is explicitly selected before analysis and within source max strain 0.05 for compression
Yield is first qualified peak before densification, not global maximum
MD/CD baseline material normalization is direction-aware
Crosshead and DIC remain independent with alignment, calibration and uncertainty
Specimen-level mean/sample SD require at least two independent specimens; time samples/cycles never qualify
cyclic: Explicit start/turn/end segmentation; preserve signed work and residual set
Measured open-path work differs from closed-loop hysteretic loss
No forced closure for paperboard permanent set
Independent first-cycle peak reference fixed before requests; no future-value leakage
mixed: Use configuration 1 modulus and configuration 4 positive channel-area denominator separately
Channel masks and pixel-to-area transform must be independently qualified
No flow-permeability estimate from area alone
numerical: No solver or paper-exact equation implementation
Maintain theta versus pi-theta and force-axis conventions
density_scaling: Three positive relative-density groups from a=b=10,15,20 mm; five independent specimens each
Normalize modulus and first-peak strength with same-lot independently qualified MD base values
Freeze aggregation, log transform, fit weights, uncertainty propagation and support before observing data
Fit log normalized response versus log relative density; report slope/uncertainty without source exponent target
No source exact density formula until C05 has an independent qualified resolution
